sentences.text: "(I) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to release the land of the petitioner vide Khatauni Khata No.25 Gata No.30 M measuring 0.0841 hectare situating in Village Chalera Bangar, Pargana and Tehsil Dadari, District Gautam Budh Nagar as on till date neither the land has been used by the authority nor any compensation has been paid to the petitioner.

(II) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the state respondents to take appropriate decision on the application of the petitioner dated 15.06.2024 & 19.06.2024 submitted before Chief Executive Officer, Chief Administrative Office, Sector-6 NOIDA, Gautam Budh Nagar."
3. Shri Kaushalendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for Noida Authority submits that the land in dispute is acquired land.

Notification under Section 4/17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short "Old Act") was gazetted on 13.6.2008 and the notification under Section 6 read with Section 17 (1)
and 17 (4) of the Old Act was gazetted on 26.3.2009.
The actual possession was taken by the competent authority and later on the same was handed over to the Noida Authority on 11.6.2009.

It is claimed that while notifying Section 4 and 6 under the Old Act, the urgency clause under Section 17 (1) and 17 (4) of the Old Act was invoked and requirement under Section 5A of the Old Act was dispensed with.
Thereafter, possession was taken over.
It is claimed that the land is vested in the State from from all encumbrances.
The land was acquired for planned development and even the award was also made on 31.12.2013.
In this backdrop, learned counsel for Noida Authority has raised an objection that once possession of the land was taken over in the year 2009, the same cannot be divested, thereafter.

He fairly submits that as the petitioner is insisting that his claim is to be considered under the lease back policy and has confined his prayer for disposal of his applications dated 15.6.2024 & 19.6.2024, certainly the Authority would proceed to decide the said applications in accordance with law.
4. Considering the factual situation, we are not inclined to keep the matter pending consideration.

Without expressing any opinion on merits of the matter and with the consent of parties, the instant writ petition stands disposed of with observation that the aforesaid applications of the petitioner shall be considered and decided in accordance with law expeditiously.
